newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee ends steady, RBI mops up excess dlrs. [CORRECTED 14:35 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee ends steady, RBI mops up excess dlrs. [CORRECTED 14:35 GMT]

text.p: The Indian rupee ended at 35.6950/7025 against the dollar on Monday, almost unchanged from its opening level, dealers said.
There were some deals at 35.6950/75 against the dollar but most of the day's deals were at 35.70 a dollar, they said.
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) mopped up a sizeable quantity of dollars through its "passive" intervention against the backdrop of plenfitul supply, dealers said.
"I sold him (the RBI) $15 million," the chief dealer at a public sector bank said. (Corrects to $15 million from 15 million rupees)
"He did not ask for price - banks went and sold to him," he said.
The State Bank of India (SBI), India's leading commercial bank, was also selling dollars on Monday, dealers said.
"SBI was selling to the market at 35.69," a dealer said.
RBI's purchases were at 35.70 to a dollar, dealers said.

Mondays usually witness larger than average dollar supply as accumulated inward remittances from the Middle East and other markets pile up, dealers said. Dollar supply from foreign institutional investors (FIIs) buying Indian shares continued after a brief slowdown last week, dealers said.
According to latest figures released by the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE), FIIs' net purchases on the BSE amounted to 340 million rupees on July 23, the exchange said.
The rupee moved marginally against the forwar dollar.
"July to September (delivery) dollars saw some receiving (of premiums for sale of forward dollars)," said a dealer.
A private Hyderabad-based bank was a keen seller in June dollars, the chief dealer at a leading brokerage said.
The six-month annualised forward premium closed the day at 3.54 percent compared to the previous close of 3.69 percent.
